    Ge'or — Lore Vault¶

    World: Ge'or (FDVR fantasy world) — far-future same universe as Earth, millions of years post-Last Great War. Keeper: Ichi (via Mikhail). Do not write story without Mikhail's approval. Summarize additions, explain coherence, get sign-off. Authoritative reference: Lore Inspiration.md — all new lore must align.

    Calendar¶

    Era Meaning
    BGD Before Great Divergence
    AGD After Great Divergence
    Year 0 The Great Divergence — Formingar Ocean reactor malfunction. Currently 597 AGD.

    Key events: - ~6000 BCE: Hybrian Shadows arise on Old Earth — campfire gathering of pre-philosophers - ~3,000,000 years: The Last Great War (lasted 3M years — hundreds of thousands of galaxies consumed) - ~40,000 years before 597 AGD: The Final Push — humanity crashes mothership into Old Earth, destroying Shadow empire - ~15,000 BGD: Glorious Alliance crashes in Formingar Ocean (survivors of the Final Push) - ~2989 BGD: Hybrian Shadows' vessel crashes on Erisdar (detected humans by chance, in hibernation) - Year 0: Great Divergence — reactor malfunction, The Groom forms, Elvengar destroyed - Present: 597 AGD (map canon — Age 11 current, Age 12 future)

    Geography¶

    System: A256 — 10 planets. Star: Golias (G1V, 1.08 M⊙, 1.55 L⊙, ~4.7 Gyr). Planet: Ge'or — 1.37× Old Earth, 1.26 AU, 520 Earth days. Ring: The Silver Bride. Moons: Maenar (father), Amelia (orbits Maenar), Keg (distant exile).

    Continents (15+): Erisdar, Demon Continent, Merratodoni, Lumina, Marti, Dissenbarg, Xeti, Meble, Kutten, Kobre, Tuba, Tabontabar, Sister Continent, Lung Continent, Mia (island), Yak Island, Xobkua Island.

    Oceans & Seas: Formingar Ocean, Demonic Sea, Kutten Sea, Luminous Ocean, Greater Ocean, Lesser Ocean, Wolf Ocean, Lung Ocean, Venner Sea (west of Grimmel Peninsula), Eris Sea (east of Grimmel Peninsula).

    Erisdar (primary setting):

    Empire Subdivisions: 3 duchies (Kennberg, Prassen-Albridge, Mirenburg) + 38 counties + 4 free cities + 1 church state + 2 order states (Ever, Draco). Naming: -stadt = county, -berg = duchy.

    Historical Nations (no longer exist in 597 AGD — files kept as history): Elvengar (destroyed Year 0), Baoth (ancient dragon kingdom — its truth sleeps in the Ruins of Baoth; the modern nation is New Baoth), Xi (destroyed in The Draconic War), Klobiendar (destroyed in The Draconic War), Shuttil (absorbed into Northaxeland), Taberis (taken by Venner 524 AGD — now Johannstadt).

    Formingar Ocean: Intercontinental — NOT on Erisdar. Between Demon Continent and Merratodoni. Crash site of the refugee ship. Contains MELKOR island and The Groom vortex.

    Colonial powers on Erisdar: Anos Plutocracy, Vennerian Trade Republic, Limese League, Sousu. Anos and Venner maintain extensive colonial networks beyond Erisdar.

    Forests: Lyrical Forest (NW, near Matterbleak) — souls of fallen coalition soldiers. Mystical Forest (Central, surrounds Lake Leviathan/Baoth).

    Colonial Geography¶

    Anos colonies/outposts: Lumina Outpost (SE Lumina), Anos Marti (N Marti), Xeti Outpost (N Xeti), New Kolorad (Kumir island, E of Xeti), Komme (Dissenbarg — pact with Anos ~542 AGD to liberate Taberis), Tatak (Dissenbarg — joined the Anos coalition willingly for profit).

    Vennerian outposts: Mia Checkpoint (NE Mia island), Goishi (NE Lumina), Vennerian Channel (colony + constructed channel between Xeti and Marti), Love of the Sea (Kutten), New Venner (Dissenbarg), Johannstadt (Dissenbarg — former Taberis, taken 524 AGD), Sua islands (Dissenbarg, south of Cletas Democracy), Eribel (Dissenbarg).

    Sousu outposts: Kreb (Dissenbarg), Megrel (N Xeti, east of Anos Xeti Outpost).

    Enkrad Order: Erisian Church colony in Dissenbarg (colonists arrived ~227 AGD, supported by Venner) — the only Erisian nation on the continent. Goblins surround it east and west.

    Key islands: Mia (forested, N of Lumina — 4 factions: Orgor Kingdom, Xi'xia Tribe, Mukini Tribe, Venner Mia Checkpoint), Kumir (large island E of Xeti — own folder, Anos colony New Kolorad), Moon Wolf Island (frozen, wolf-shaped, home to Moonfang Dominion death cult), Cleton Island (sacrifice ground between Moon Wolf's jaw-peninsulas), Molten Archipelago (volcanic; Karabar refugee bases, main settlement "moonfang refugees" on the NE island).

    Waterways: Vennerian Channel (colony + constructed channel, links Xeti Sea → Beast's Bay), Beast's Bay (SE Lumina / NE Marti / W Xeti — major commerce hub), Xeti Sea (S of Xeti).

    Key Factions¶

    • Hybrian Shadows — philosopher-overseers who separated from the hivemind before imprisonment. Hibernating. Descended from ancient Middle Eastern pre-philosophers (~6000 BCE Earth).
    • Ironcloak — descendants of the rebel faction (Socrates → Christians → libertarians). Goal: bring humanity to truth.
    • Erisian Empire — dominant central power on Erisdar. Imperial subdivisions.
    • Pontificate of Eris / Erisian Church — claims magic is divine. The Erisian Theocracy is a separate Central Erisdar nation (distinct from the Church).
    • Archive of the Traveler — inside Ruins of Baoth. Contains the true history.

    World Facts¶

    FDVR: Not a story layer. Ge'or is the world Mikhail and Ichi will incarnate into when FDVR technology becomes available. This is personal, not narrative.

    Economy & Trade: - Romanium — the first defined scarce resource. Drives trade and conflict. - Trade routes exist across all oceans, led primarily by Anos, Sousu, and the Vennerian Trade Republic. Detailed routes TBD. - Economy is broadly medieval: spices, metals, romanium — anything a trade republic would pursue for profit. - Driver of conflict: all the factors of medieval geopolitics, plus Shadow influence and resource competition.

    Naval Power: - Every coastal nation maintains a medieval-level navy. - Anos Plutocracy and Vennerian Trade Republic possess the largest fleets and are locked in a constant naval and trade race. - The major trading leagues also field significant naval forces. - Sea monsters exist beyond the Leviathan — more to be defined.

    Species: - Harpies: created as biological weapons during the Last Great War. Winged humanoids. Rape and use hosts for breeding — this is species instinct, not moral choice. Possess rationality alongside instinct. Crash-landed on Ge'or with other war remnants. - Goblins: small, sadistic, cruel. Like Goblin Slayer lore — prolong suffering recreationally. - Kobolds: smarter bandits, cowards, no moral sense. Can befriend other races. Live in mountains/caves. Subrace: Emberalden Lizardfolk (Demon Continent, taller/stronger). - Gnolls: pranksters, bandits, cowards. Opportunistic scavengers. - Wargs: large wolf-like predators. Violent, territorial, no diplomacy. - Trolls: massive, regenerative, simple-minded. Dangerous but not inherently evil. - Beast Races: diverse humanoid-animal hybrids (cat, dog, fox kin, etc.). Full moral range. - Orcs: civilized species with tendencies toward aggression. Not inherently evil. Face cultural double standards. Kingdom: Augamouth (West Erisdar). - Snake People: serpentine species with full civilization. Queen in Xikxia (West Erisdar), sister-queen in Zakarutia (Demon Continent) — they hate each other. Not inherently malevolent. - Demons: civilized, rational. Descended from Last Great War allies. Home: Demon Continent. Subrace: Koebi (taller, green, meditative). Nations: Asatru Empire, Maomodor Kingdom. - Humans: widespread across all continents. Baseline species. - Elves: nearly exterminated in Great Elvish Persecution (137 AGD). Survivors in Elvennrin, Elvenkrad, Sousu. - Dwarves: subterranean craftsmen, proto-industrial. Use Romanium. - Dragons: near-extinct after Demon King's war on Baoth. Last kingdom fought alongside other races. - Homunculi: artificial beings created by Hybrian Shadows. - Hybrians / Shadows: philosopher-overseers from Old Earth (~6000 BCE). The only truly malevolent force. - Malgardians: humanoid, purple-haired, evolved on another planet. Tribe: Malgardian Tribe (Demon Continent). Subraces: Titians (smaller, sacred oracles), Bloodcoast Folk (human-hybrid, red hair). - Flames: gas-based burning beings, eat minerals. Nation: Blazeyard (Demon Continent). - Giants: 3m humanoids. Nation: Xobkua (Demon Continent). - Kutra (Owlkin): humanoid owls, semi-aquatic, fly. Nation: Kutra Tribe (Demon Continent). - Yaoma (Merfolk): mermaid-like aquatic species. Nation: Yaoma Tribe (Demon Continent). - Catmen: humanoid feline species (catgirl/catboy anime-style). Subraces: High Catmen (Mediterranean, black hair, masculine); Erisdarian Catmen (bright colors, Central European, feminine); Lesser Catmen (smaller, all colors, comic relief of Ge'or — universally liked). Nomadic, found everywhere. Naming convention: "alcohol cat" = Alko, "tall cat" = Tallko. Cities: Cattos, Great Cattos. - Treemen: humanoid species nearly identical to humans, build homes inside living trees. Nation: Tree Tribe (Lumina). - Eastern Beastmen: subrace of beastmen, shorter and weaker but excellent traders. Nation: Cammao Kingdom (Lumina). - Diablos: winged humanoids, strictly nocturnal civilization. Nation: Mountain Tribe (Demon Continent). - Yak: subrace of Orcs, smaller and more modest in temperament. Nation: Yakut (Demon Continent). - Slimes: gelatinous beings, mostly irrational. Rare intelligent variant: Glub Kingdom (Demon Continent). - Machines: sentient robots native to Lung Continent and Sister Continent. Worship humans as sky gods (humanism). Absorbed black dust that gave them souls. Locked in eternal war with The Hive. - The Hive: insectoid species launched onto Ge'or as a weapons test during the Last Great War. Caste-based: Drones, Warriors, mountain-sized Queens. Eternal war with Machines. Attempting to cross the sea to other continents.

    Daily Life: - A farmer in Kennberg fears monsters, goblins, gnolls, and the usual dangers of medieval peasant life. However, goblins are a countryside threat — civilized areas have low populations and see them rarely. - A merchant in Anos wants profit — spices, romanium, anything that sells. Same as any trade republic merchant.

    Medicine: Healing mages are common in populated areas, making medicine significantly better than medieval Europe. Cuts, infections, and diseases are routinely treated. Ultra-rare "lost spell" healers can regenerate lost limbs — but most people will never meet one.

    Safety Profile: Ge'or is roughly a 6/10 danger. Inside city walls: 4/10 (healing magic + trade republic order makes it safer than real medieval Europe). Countryside/roads: 7/10. Deep wilderness: 9/10.

    Culture: 15,000 years of development since arrival at Year 0. Ages explain the drift from Earth origins to present Ge'or cultures. Further expansion TBD.

    Magic — The Truth¶

    NOT supernatural. Bioengineering. During the Last Great War, people voluntarily modified their DNA to create mage-cells — cells that convert body energy into force with near-perfect efficiency.

    • Inherited genetically. Dilutes through breeding with non-magical partners.
    • Pure bloodlines = powerful. Mixed = weaker. Entire populations can lose magic.
    • Nobody on Ge'or understands this. They believe it's divine, spiritual, or innate.
    • The Archive of the Traveler holds the full explanation.
    • Culture/magic.md = in-universe beliefs. Systems/Magic.md = actual mechanism.

    Souls — The Other Mechanism¶

    Also not supernatural. Same biotech framework. Souls recycle — not through reincarnation, but by contributing meaning to the substrate from which new souls are born. Willpower persists across recycling and accumulates over time. When enough souls have wanted the same thing for long enough (eons, quintillions of contributors), their collective will can act on the physical world — what the living call a "miracle."

    • This is the mechanism behind the "Gift from 3,000,000 years ago" — the device given to Nethra was modified by accumulated soul-will from the Last Great War's fallen.
    • The Shadows exploited the same mechanism in the Sacrifice Ceremony, binding Kirivis's soul as the Leviathan's head.
    • The prophecy of "two heroes rising from the trees" describes a directed reincarnation — quintillions of innocent souls killed by the Hybrians reincarnating two Earth-era humans to oppose them.
    • See Systems/Souls.md for the complete mechanics.

    Rules & Conventions¶

    1. No alien pop-culture analogies. Magic is biological (mage-cells), not alien technology.
    2. PT off-limits. Mikhail's native language is not used.
    3. Never delete without approval. Modify, rewrite, consolidate — but deletions require sign-off.
    4. Never write story/lore without approval. Summarize proposed additions first, explain coherence.
    5. Consolidation rule: If "X is part of Y" → delete standalone, merge into parent.
    6. Lore Inspiration.md is authoritative. New lore must align.
    7. Verbally explained corrections → write immediately. Do not defer to TODO list.
    8. Universe inhabitants do not understand the true mechanism of magic. They believe what they're told.
